svg.title: One inquiry, one auditable settlement
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-inbound-auction-to-collected-cash; chart type: process_flow; title: One inquiry, one auditable settlement; subtitle: Separate routing speed from qualification evidence and cash collection.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Illustrative operating sequence for directly contracted publishers and buyers. Ringba or Retreaver timeout settings are tested against actual buyer response times; sub-second bidding is an engineering target, not an asserted service level. A 90–120 second threshold is a negotiated billing condition, never evidence of lawful contact.; caption: Preserve a shared call identifier from source click through buyer payment; a winning bid alone does not establish collectible revenue.; stages: label: Capture source and permission; value: Bind click, caller, disclosure, and intended recipient; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Persist source campaign, landing-page version, timestamp, recipient identity, and TrustedForm or Jornaya evidence where applicable. A certificate records evidence; it does not independently establish valid permission.; label: Validate inquiry and eligibility; value: Check geography, duplication, contact rules, and capacity; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Confirm service intent, buyer coverage, business hours, and duplicate-call lookback. For regulated outbound follow-up, apply current suppression and permission rules. A commercial litigation-risk list never substitutes for National or entity-specific DNC controls.; label: Ping eligible contracted buyers; value: Auction minimal attributes against live caps; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Send only contractually permitted routing attributes. Apply Ringba or Retreaver bid timeouts, geographic filters, capacity limits, and a fallback route; avoid broadcasting the caller's identity to every bidder.; label: Post and qualify the connection; value: Connect once and measure contracted connected seconds; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Select the eligible bid, connect the caller, and measure the buyer-agreed 90–120 second buffer using the agreed clock. Distinguish ringing, hold time, and agent-connected time; review transcript classifications before billing.; label: Reconcile and collect; value: Resolve scrubs before increasing publisher exposure; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Match disposition, duration, duplicate status, invoice, and bank receipt by call identifier. Keep publisher caps tight until actual net-7 buyer collections are verified; send S2S value corrections when accepted calls reverse.

Assumptions: Illustrative operating sequence for directly contracted publishers and buyers. Ringba or Retreaver timeout settings are tested against actual buyer response times; sub-second bidding is an engineering target, not an asserted service level. A 90–120 second threshold is a negotiated billing condition, never evidence of lawful contact.
